races.name: Zyn Frontrunner EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Zyn Strong Stride EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Date Line
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's filly is the race's sole confirmed front-runner, has handled Good going in both career starts going 1W 1P, and steps up to a mile for the first time after two 7f runs — Callum Shepherd takes the ride on a 420-day absence that is the primary unknown, and fast conditions suit her profile entirely.

runners_data.name: Evening Call
runners_data.note: Haggas has the resources to send out a well-schooled debutante, but Evening Call's running style is wholly unknown and she arrives with a blank form record, meaning she is mapped to the rear by default rather than genuine hold-up inclination — watch for how she travels early as the key read.

runners_data.name: Gilding The Lily
runners_data.note: Robert Havlin partnering for Gosden on a filly who finished second on her sole start at Sandown 14 days ago keeps her race-fit edge, and a prominent racing style means she is best positioned to shadow Date Line and capitalise on any late weakness rather than make a ground-making challenge.

races.paceDynamic: Date Line is the sole confirmed front-runner in a three-horse field and will stride to the front unchallenged from the outset, setting a controlled, unhurried gallop over the Newmarket July mile on Good to Firm ground. Gilding The Lily is likely to track closely in a prominent position, meaning Date Line faces no genuine pressure to accelerate the tempo against her will. Evening Call, whose style is unknown but redistributed to the rear, will be held up at the back of this tiny field, making up the tail of a procession rather than exerting any forcing influence. This race shape — a lone, uncontested lead on a flat, galloping track with fast ground — strongly favours the front-runner and prominent types who can dictate their own rhythm, conserve energy through the race, and repel challengers in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Date Line Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Date Line dictates a smooth, sustainable gallop and finds enough in the tank to repel challengers in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Date Line sets every fraction on her own terms on fast ground she handles well, building a rhythm that turns this into a test of stamina and composure over the mile trip; her two career runs at 7f on Good suggest the step up to a mile is the logical next move and she has the class to see it out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Closer Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If Date Line goes too hard too soon and Gilding The Lily, tracking closely, pounces in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A pace-strung small field can sometimes see the front-runner overdo it slightly, leaving Gilding The Lily perfectly poised to swoop as Date Line ties up; Gosden's filly brings the benefit of a recent outing 14 days ago, keeping her sharp and ready to capitalise on any front-runner weakness.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Evening Call Sweeps Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final quarter-mile and Evening Call, tracking from the rear, finds clear daylight to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: With only three runners the hold-up position is barely a length off the pace, so Evening Call needs the first two to exhaust each other before producing her run; given her unknown style and lightly raced profile under Haggas, an ability to unleash a powerful late turn of foot cannot be dismissed entirely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Dead Rubber Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If all three fillies arrive in a cluster turning for home and the race is settled by fine margins of finishing speed.
scenarios.body: A tight, uninspiring gallop with no pressure could compress the field so thoroughly that class differentials are nullified and fractional advantages in the final 100 yards decide the outcome; any of the three could feature, but this scenario requires Date Line to sacrifice her natural front-running advantage by underperforming.

watchPoints.text: Date Line returns from a 420-day absence — watch her paddock demeanour and early jumping, as any rustiness under Shepherd could undermine her expected front-running supremacy.

Gilding The Lily is the only runner with meaningful recent form (14 days ago), and if she is able to sit a length off Date Line through the first six furlongs, she becomes a serious threat in the final two.
Evening Call's unknown racing style is the biggest wildcard — if she breaks sharply and contests the early lead, it transforms an otherwise processional pace map into a genuinely pressured contest.

The going for this race is confirmed Good to Firm at the July course, faster than the headline Good figure, which will magnify the advantage of a front-runner who can roll along at a fluent, economical tempo without burning reserves.

With only three runners, positional tactics are almost irrelevant — watch instead for which filly shows superior cruising speed in the final quarter-mile, as that is likely to be the decisive factor in this small-field novice.

races.name: Maritime Cargo Sts Freight Frenzy Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Sir Edward Lear
runners_data.note: Prominent runner stepping back in trip from 12f-plus assignments, with recent form showing consistency in the 3-5 range on Good ground; the visor is fitted and James Owen's runner has the profile to sit just off Triggerman and battle out a finish, though the return to 1m after longer campaigns is the key question.

runners_data.name: Calyxoh
runners_data.note: Form figures of 097304 suggest unreliability, but ran only 12 days ago and retains freshness; a genuine hold-up type who needs things to fall right from the rear, and Dylan Hogan will require luck in running on a straight course where getting boxed in is a real risk.
runners_data.comment: Calyxoh shaped well enough with a third three starts back and returns in good order on 12 days' rest, handling today's distance and going with experience; winless in recent starts, he nonetheless rates highest of the eight and is the one to beat off 133 lb from stall 5.

runners_data.name: The Sweet Escape
runners_data.note: In excellent recent form with back-to-back wins at this trip and track conditions, making her the standout exposed form horse among the prominent types; Laura Pearson's mount handles Good to Firm well (3W5P in similar going) and a forward position off Triggerman's pace plays directly to her strengths.
runners_data.comment: The Sweet Escape arrives on the back of back-to-back wins, and a close second last time out keeps him firmly in form; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 131 lb from stall 2 is the chief weight to overcome.

runners_data.name: Special Ghaiyyath
runners_data.note: Moderate recent form with figures of 368974 and a true hold-up style that the field shape has pushed into a midfield mapping; a 0.94 style-fit flag signals she is racing out of her natural role here, and while the going is fine, her chance is best viewed as limited unless the race falls apart completely.
runners_data.comment: Special Ghaiyyath brings strong fitness credentials having run just 16 days ago, and has experience of both today's trip and conditions, while our rating of 76 marks him out as a live threat from stall one; the concern is he remains winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Currumbin
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse most effective over longer trips (multiple 12f-16f runs in the history), racing here over a shorter 1m than ideal; the redistribution to midfield reflects a crowded hold-up division, and Harry Davies will need to find the equivalent of a sprint finish that rarely suits this type's profile.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with an unplaced effort three starts back and only a fourth two starts back to show recently, Currumbin carries 123 lb from stall four and, ranked last on our figures, makes little appeal despite having experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Triggerman
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner who should dictate on a straight, flat mile with no obvious challenger for the early lead; form figures of 39-680 on good-ish ground are modest, but the ability to control fractions on Newmarket's July course gives him a tactical advantage his bare figures don't advertise.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked seventh of eight on our figures, Triggerman is hard to fancy despite the experience over today's distance and going; a well-beaten eighth two starts back and unplaced latest make it difficult to make a case, though 22 days off and a return to familiar conditions offer slim encouragement.

runners_data.name: Rising Force
runners_data.note: Highest OR in the field at 74 and a strong recent form line including a win and a second over this trip on Good ground; Marco Ghiani is an experienced operator who will hunt the gaps late, and if any horse can produce a telling late thrust it is this one, though the straight course still demands a clear run.
runners_data.comment: Second last time out gives Rising Force a live each-way claim, though a fifth and fourth in the two runs before that effort suggest he was some way off it; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 14 days between runs keeps him fresh enough to factor from stall 3.

runners_data.name: Mr Ubiquitous
runners_data.note: Progressive profile off a career-best win (1/7f/STA) with four wins from his last ten runs and the highest combined strike-rate in similar going (10/15); Kaiya Fraser rides for Harry Eustace and the prominent style suits the likely race shape perfectly, making this runner's tactical profile among the most aligned to the dominant scenario.
runners_data.comment: Fifth last time out and a winner four starts back, Mr Ubiquitous brings distance and going experience to the table, but his recent form is patchy and carrying 134 lb from stall 8 leaves plenty to prove at a mark of 73.

races.paceDynamic: Triggerman is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner mile handicap and, with no rival likely to press him hard from the gates, he should establish an uncontested lead and set a controlled, measured tempo on the Newmarket July course straight. The three prominent types — Sir Edward Lear, The Sweet Escape and Mr Ubiquitous — will settle just off the pace and are well placed to pounce if Triggerman's fractions are honest but not punishing. The field carries more hold-up horses than the race shape can naturally accommodate at the rear: Special Ghaiyyath and Currumbin are genuine closers but have been redistributed to midfield in the map, meaning Rising Force — the highest-rated of the hold-up horses — is the one true closer most likely to find clear ground late. A controlled, single-pace gallop set by an uncontested Triggerman strongly favours prominent racers who can travel sweetly just behind the leader and strike decisively in the final two furlongs, with the pace too honest to allow a strong late flourish from deep.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Raiders Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Triggerman leads at an honest but unforced gallop and the prominent trio track him into the straight.
scenarios.body: Triggerman sets a rhythmical tempo that suits horses sitting just off the pace, and Sir Edward Lear, The Sweet Escape or Mr Ubiquitous each have the tactical position to peel off his quarters and quicken clear; Good to Firm ground rewards that forward-placed, travelling style.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Gallops Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Triggerman is allowed to dictate completely unchallenged and the prominent horses fail to close down his advantage rounding into the Dip.
scenarios.body: An uncontested Triggerman can find a comfortable rhythm and conserve enough energy to sustain his effort through the final furlong on quick ground; none of the hold-up horses behind him has a clear enough run to bridge the gap in time.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or the prominent runners fail to quicken, leaving a gap for a horse delivered late from midfield.
scenarios.body: Rising Force, the highest-rated runner in the field, is best placed among the closers to pick up late on Good to Firm ground if there is a genuine tempo; Special Ghaiyyath and Currumbin are mapped out of their truest role and face an uphill task finding clear daylight from deep in a straight-course mile.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Bunched Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Triggerman goes too steady and the race turns into a sprint finish off a slow tempo with the field arriving in a heap.
scenarios.body: A falsely run race compresses the entire field entering the final two furlongs, giving higher-rated horses like Rising Force and Mr Ubiquitous a chance to use raw ability rather than position; the lack of true pace punishes horses whose form depends on a searching gallop drawing the sting from rivals.

watchPoints.text: Triggerman's early gallop sets the entire tempo — watch whether Finlay Bassett (7) allows him to coast or is bustled along, because any increase in early fractions immediately shifts the advantage away from the front-runner and toward the prominent trio.

The Sweet Escape's barrier draw and Laura Pearson's positioning in the opening furlong are critical — if she is shuffled back behind a wall of horses rather than tracking Triggerman's quarters directly, her recent winning momentum counts for less.

Rising Force is the one genuine closer with the class to win, but Marco Ghiani must find daylight on a straight course with eight runners — watch the early stages to see whether he can slot onto the rail or is forced wide, which will determine whether his late effort is a threat or a near-miss.

Special Ghaiyyath and Currumbin are both natural hold-up horses mapped into midfield due to congestion at the rear — if both attempt to drop back to their comfort zone from the gates, they risk being detached and effectively out of the race before the turn into the Dip.

Mr Ubiquitous has strong course form over 7f at Newmarket and steps to 1m — watch whether he relaxes behind the pace in the early stages or pulls for his head, as his four-win recent strike-rate is built on getting a smooth first half to the race.

races.name: Maritime Cargo Sts Container Storage Solutions Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Fifty Nifty
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer whose sole win came over this exact 6f trip on good ground; Callum Shepherd partners a horse that needs a strong pace to run into, and the Romantic Twilight/Beauzon duel sets that up perfectly — seven days since last run is sharp enough.
runners_data.comment: Fifty Nifty bounced back to winning form last time out and, carrying 145 lb from stall two, he has experience of both today's trip and conditions; the inconsistency in recent starts is a mild reservation, but on a mark of 70 he looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Mumayaz
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old veteran with five consecutive 6f good-ground runs showing consistent form; Tony Carroll sends this horse in decent shape (5/45 last 14 days) and his hold-up style is well suited to a contested pace, though a modest recent string of placed efforts without a win is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Mumayaz showed his best when winning five starts back, but has failed to recapture that form since, finishing no better than third in his last four outings; he has run over today's trip and going, returns after 22 days, and carries 140 lb from stall 11.

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Condor
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who showed a placed effort last time at Sandown; apprentice Shay Farmer (5lb claim) is a genuine tactical advantage in a big field, and the horse's good-to-firm form figures (4/15) warrant some caution, but the style is right for this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Consistent in defeat but knocking hard on the door, Ziggy's Condor brings strong recent placing form — second last time out and third two starts back — and has run over today's trip and going, with our rating of 77 marking him a leading threat; the main risk is that he remains yet to win in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Jenny
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent runner who has placed four times from her last five efforts across good and standard ground; Dougie Costello is a strong booking for a horse that likes to sit close to the pace, and the yard (Hollinshead) has no winners in the last 14 days which is a mild flag.
runners_data.comment: Ran second two starts back and won three starts back, so Spirit Of Jenny clearly has ability, but that eighth last time out is a concern; she has run over today's trip and going, and 138 lb from stall six makes this a stiff ask at a rating of 68.

runners_data.name: Northcliff
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who handles good ground well with a recent second over this course and distance; wears a visor which can sharpen focus, and the 13-day turnaround from Ross Burdon's stable (0/8 last 14 days) doesn't inspire training-form confidence despite the horse's solid individual record.
runners_data.comment: Northcliff finished second last time out and has experience of both today's trip and going, with 13 days' rest leaving him primed on fitness; the concern is that he has found only one win in his last six starts, suggesting he can be vulnerable when it matters most.

runners_data.name: Beauzon
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner whose form figures on good-to-firm (2/15) are markedly inferior to his standard/soft ground record; Ryan Kavanagh (3lb claim) riding, but the key concern is that his recent wins at Sandown came on softer ground and Newmarket July on good-to-firm is a very different test — he will likely press or lead, but burning himself out is a real risk.
runners_data.comment: Beauzon has won three times in his last six starts, showing a clear ability to hit the front, but back-to-back unplaced efforts since dampen enthusiasm; he has experience over today's trip and going, and 20 days between runs suggests freshness, though 137 lb from stall 12 is no easy ask.

runners_data.name: Rebel Path
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse wearing a hood (hg:p) with two thirds in his last five runs showing he can threaten without winning; Chloe Lyons (7lb claim) is a significant claim in a field this competitive, and his good-to-firm record (9/15) is solid enough that he warrants respect in the late-finisher category.
runners_data.comment: Rebel Path shaped with promise when third last time out and returns on a quick turnaround of just 14 days, with experience over today's trip and conditions working in his favour; our rating of 77 marks him as a strong danger, though he remains winless in recent starts and will need to find more to get his head in front.

runners_data.name: Romantic Twilight
runners_data.note: The other confirmed pace-setter, three-year-old with his sole win over this course and trip on good ground; William Stone has had no winners in 14 days and the lightly-raced profile (16-095 recent form) shows inconsistency, but the raw speed to lead is not in doubt — the question is whether the pace war with Beauzon leaves him with nothing in reserve.
runners_data.comment: Romantic Twilight showed she can win, landing victory five starts back, but has struggled since, finishing no better than fifth in her last four starts. She has run over today's distance and going before, returns after 23 days, and carries 134 lb from stall 7.

runners_data.name: Currahee
runners_data.note: Prominent to midfield type who wears a hood and tongue-tie (hg:tp); Marco Ghiani is an upgrade in the saddle, and his one win came at 7f on standard ground meaning the combination of 6f and good-to-firm is slightly against him based on history (6/13 in similar going).
runners_data.comment: Beaten in four of his last five starts, with a ninth and eighth in recent starts making him hard to fancy here, and our figures rank him ninth of twelve in the field; the win five starts back offers slim hope, and he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Bayraat
runners_data.note: Consistent placed horse whose record shows 1W6P from 12 runs on similar going — a genuinely strong hold-up type; Tom Tate has had no activity in 14 days, and because the field is packed with true closers, Bayraat is mapped to midfield rather than the rear, meaning his natural finishing kick may be partially compromised by having to run closer to the pace than ideal.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and carrying 127 lb from stall nine, Bayraat is hard to fancy on the back of an unplaced effort last time out, though he has winning form in recent starts and has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Molly Mac
runners_data.note: Three-year-old prominent runner who won last time over this exact 6f trip on good ground; Grace McEntee rides for Micky Fenton (1/2 last 14 days, a warm yard stat), and the horse's consistent placed record suggests she handles varying conditions — a lightly-weighted dark horse in the prominent camp.
runners_data.comment: Ranked tenth of twelve on our figures, Molly Mac faces a stiff ask against stronger company, but she does arrive on the back of a win last time out and has experience of today's trip and going, which counts for something.

runners_data.name: Em Jay Kay
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer by profile whose natural style is swept toward the rear, yet here is mapped to midfield due to the volume of closers in the field; Phil McEntee's charge has a tongue-tie (hg:p), 31 days off (longest in the field), and all recent form figures come on standard ground at Southwell/Wolverhampton, making the good-to-firm Newmarket surface a significant unknown.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 11 of 12 on our figures, Em Jay Kay makes little appeal after four poor efforts in his last four starts, though a win five starts back shows he can find the winning post and he has experience of today's distance and going.

races.paceDynamic: Romantic Twilight and Beauzon are the two confirmed front-runners, and both will want to lead from the outset on this straight Newmarket July course over six furlongs, creating a genuinely contested early gallop rather than any dawdle. With Beauzon's recent form showing a string of wins on soft/standard ground but only modest form on good-to-firm (2/15 in similar going), and Romantic Twilight also limited in similar-going records (8/10 but with late faders in those splits), their duel is likely to set an honest, pressured tempo from the off. This contested pace suits hold-up and late-finishing profiles who can sit off the speed, let the front pair burn each other out, and pick up through the final two furlongs. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Bayraat and Em Jay Kay are genuine closers forced into midfield slots on the map because the true hold-up berths are oversubscribed, meaning Fifty Nifty, Mumayaz, Northcliff and Rebel Path are the likely authentic hold-up runners on the day. The race shape strongly favours hold-up and midfield-to-late runners who can produce a sustained finish once the front pair have done their work.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Pair Burn Out
scenarios.trigger: If Romantic Twilight and Beauzon press each other hard from the gate, setting a strong contested gallop that empties both by the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The honest pace drains both leaders in the final 150 yards, opening the door for genuine closers tracking behind them to storm through. Hold-up horses with proven good-to-firm form like Fifty Nifty and Northcliff are best placed to capitalise on the energy expenditure at the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent-style runners settles just off the pace and pounces as the leaders fade in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Spirit Of Jenny or Ziggy's Condor could sit a length or two off the front, conserving enough energy to pick up when the front-runners tire. On good-to-firm ground at Newmarket, a smooth prominent run with a single change of gear is a well-worn winning formula at this track.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Leader Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner (most likely Romantic Twilight) gains a clear early advantage and the other fails to match strides, allowing a solo controlled lead.
scenarios.body: A lone leader who controls fractions on good-to-firm can produce a surprisingly resilient performance, particularly over this straight six furlongs where no bends break momentum. Romantic Twilight's one win came in this style and the track and conditions are compatible, though the presence of Beauzon makes a truly uncontested lead unlikely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Fail To Land Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves only moderate despite two nominal leaders, with the field bunching and hold-up horses failing to generate the clear run and momentum they need.
scenarios.body: True hold-up types like Bayraat and Em Jay Kay are already mapped out of their ideal position and are racing in a compromised role, reducing the probability of a deep late flourish working. In this scenario the race is won from a stalking position mid-pack rather than from the rear, and the honest closers are left with too much ground to make up through the straight.

watchPoints.text: Beauzon and Romantic Twilight — watch the first furlong closely; if both are hard ridden immediately, the pace is genuinely strong and the hold-up runners (Fifty Nifty, Northcliff) move sharply upward in winning expectation.

Bayraat and Em Jay Kay are true hold-up types mapped to midfield — if they get shuffled back to their natural position early in the race, they will have significantly more ground to make up than the pace map implies.

Em Jay Kay has been off 31 days, the longest break in the field, with all recent form on artificial surfaces — watch for any market drift at the off as an indicator the ground is catching connections cold.

Molly Mac — watch for Grace McEntee to position prominently early; a lightly-weighted three-year-old last seen winning at this trip and course configuration represents a plausible price-to-ability mismatch in the prominent-stalker scenario.

Northcliff's visor fitting is worth monitoring in the paddock — headgear horses can either be sharper or more fractious, and a settled pre-race demeanour would be a positive signal for his hold-up chance if the front-runners set the expected strong gallop.

races.name: Racing TV Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: God Of War
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist returning after 100 days off for Tom Clover, who has a solid 5/17 T14 record; the layoff is a concern but recent form shows a win and two placings on good ground at the right trip, and he needs a strong pace to deliver his late run — this race gives him that if the prominent cluster runs hard early.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and absent for 100 days, God Of War faces questions on freshness, though he has run over today's distance and going and a rating of 94 offers mild encouragement from stall ten carrying 138 lb.

runners_data.name: Sterling Knight
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's seven-year-old is lightly raced recently (13d) and posts excellent similar-going figures (9/15, 1W4P), and at 8f on Good ground he's essentially at home; the 7lb claimer Toby Moore is a consideration, but Sterling Knight's consistent prominent style means he's well-suited to travel just off Brocklesby Bill without wasting energy in the early scrimmage.
runners_data.comment: Sterling Knight shaped with promise when third two starts back, but was unplaced either side of that effort and could manage only seventh last time out; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 93 gives him a chance off 137 lb from stall four.

runners_data.name: Principality
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's four-year-old won last time at this trip on Good and has placed twice in similar conditions (9/15), so the ground holds no fears; returning after 70 days, Kaiya Fraser rides, and as a hold-up type Principality needs the pace to be genuine — the congested prominent group makes that plausible.
runners_data.comment: Principality won two starts back but has been out of the frame since, and 70 days off the track raises a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going, and carries 136 lb from stall one.

runners_data.name: Zarathos
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha's four-year-old carries the best similar-going figures in the field (11/15, 2W6P) and has won twice at 8f on good ground recently; Callum Shepherd takes the ride, and as a hold-up horse Zarathos ideally wants the prominent traffic to burn hot before unleashing his finish — his recent course and distance experience gives him strong claims.
runners_data.comment: Zarathos comes into this unplaced last time out and ranks eighth of ten on our figures, making him hard to fancy at the weights. He does arrive fit on a 16-day turnaround, has experience over today's trip and going, and back-to-back wins four and five starts back show ability, but recent form makes appeal difficult.

runners_data.name: Croupier
runners_data.note: This seven-year-old is a natural prominent racer — confirmed by his past-post positions — but with four horses competing for three spots ahead of him, he is unlikely to access his preferred pitch; Joel Parkinson & Sue Smith send him here on 13 days' rest and the Style Fit tag (0.92) reflects that racing further back than usual will blunt his chance, particularly on a course where position matters.
runners_data.comment: Croupier shaped well when third last time out and that placed effort, combined with his experience over today's trip and going, makes him a leading threat under 135 lb; the main concern is that he remains yet to win in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Brocklesby Bill
runners_data.note: The only genuine front-runner in the field, this three-year-old won here over 8f on Good last time for apprentice Charlie Tucker, and his handful of similar-going starts (4/5, 2W3P) confirm he thrives on quick ground; the absence of any rival willing or able to press him is decisive for the shape of this race, though his head gear (h) warrants monitoring for early behaviour.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of ten on our figures, Brocklesby Bill faces a stiff task under 125 lb from stall nine, yet he has run over today's trip and going before and arrives in fair nick with two wins in his last five starts, including a win last time out.

runners_data.name: Mythical Guest
runners_data.note: George Margarson's six-year-old has never won on similar going across 11 attempts and has been held up in rear throughout recent form — a genuine back-end runner who needs the field to come back to him; the redistribution reflects the race's crowded midfield, but his 0W3P similar-going record at this trip and Mason Paetel's 5lb claim make him a tail-end risk rather than a serious threat.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked ninth of ten on our figures, Mythical Guest faces a stiff ask here, though a third two starts back and experience over today's trip and going offer slim encouragement; drawn in stall two and back after 27 days.

runners_data.name: Storm Star
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's five-year-old tops the weights and carries a 57d absence, but his only comparable recent piece — a second at 8f on Good — shows he can perform fresh; his similar-going record is thin (4/15, 0W3P), and while Alfie Redman (7) takes the ride, Storm Star needs to secure a prominent berth before the traffic bunches two out or his chance evaporates.
runners_data.comment: Storm Star shaped with promise when second two starts back and his experience over today's trip and going counts in his favour, but he has been winless in recent starts and the 57-day absence is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Hickory
runners_data.note: This eight-year-old is a course winner over 8f on Good and his similar-going figures (12/15, 2W5P) are the strongest in the race for any horse wanting a prominent position; headgear (p) has been worn before and clearly suits, William Carver rides, and Hickory's ability to travel close to the pace while conserving energy for a late thrust makes him the most naturally suited to the dominant race shape.
runners_data.comment: Hickory arrives on the back of a win last time out and looks well-placed to go again, handling both today's trip and going with experience to call upon; the main concern is that his recent record shows some inconsistency, with four defeats in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Tuscan Hills
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's four-year-old has a moderate similar-going record (6/9, 1W1P) and his recent form at the trip has been uninspiring, finishing fifth twice on Good; Rob Hornby rides and Tuscan Hills is a prominent type who needs a clean passage off Brocklesby Bill's pace, but his recent course and trip form leaves him with something to prove at this level.
runners_data.comment: Tuscan Hills has run over today's trip and going before, and a 13-day turnaround keeps him fresh; winless in his last five starts, a fifth last time out at least shows consistency, and 140 lb from stall three gives him a workable weight and draw to build on.

races.paceDynamic: Brocklesby Bill is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should settle into a comfortable, uncontested rhythm on Good to Firm ground over Newmarket's straight mile — a surface and track configuration that historically rewards horses who can control tempo without burning energy. Behind him, Storm Star, Hickory, Tuscan Hills and Sterling Knight all want prominent positions, creating a four-way scramble for the two or three spots just off the pace between the two-furlong and three-furlong markers, where traffic and interference become a real threat. The hold-up brigade of God Of War, Zarathos and Principality will need that prominent congestion to unwind cleanly before they can deliver their finishing kicks from off the pace. This race shape — a single uncontested leader controlling a genuinely honest gallop ahead of a packed mid-division — clearly favours prominent racers who can travel just behind the pace and pounce before the hold-up horses get organised; the field contains more prominent types than can all find their natural slot, and of those chasing the early positions, Storm Star (recent 1m form) and Hickory (course winner, headgear) are best-placed to actually secure a berth, with Sterling Knight also capable of dictating his own fate from just off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Brocklesby Bill dictates an honest but uncontested pace and the prominent horses track him cleanly without burning out in early scrimmaging.
scenarios.body: Brocklesby Bill sets a metronomic gallop, Hickory or Storm Star travel sweetly just behind and have enough in reserve to collar him inside the final furlong on fast ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Hold-Up Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If Brocklesby Bill crawls and the prominent pack sits too close, compressing the race and leaving a wall of horses two out.
scenarios.body: A slow early tempo bunches the field and sets up a sprint finish from the two-furlong pole, giving the hold-up horses a genuine gap to attack through late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage Blows Race Open
scenarios.trigger: If the four prominent types clash aggressively for position early, inflating the pace and stringing out the field.
scenarios.body: Brocklesby Bill is pressured into a genuine gallop, the prominent horses who burned petrol fade in the final furlong, and a fresh-legged hold-up horse picks up the pieces.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Bias Delivers Lone Front-Runner
scenarios.trigger: If Good to Firm conditions and a clear early lead allow Brocklesby Bill to dictate every yard and the field fails to close.
scenarios.body: Brocklesby Bill, unchallenged and relaxed, builds an insurmountable advantage entering the final two furlongs on quick ground that rewards front-runners who get a soft lead.

watchPoints.text: Brocklesby Bill (Charlie Tucker, 7lb claimer) — if the apprentice lets him bowl along unchallenged from flag fall, he sets the entire race tempo and any drift in early fractions will scramble the tactics of all four prominent horses behind him.

Prominent scrimmage between Storm Star, Hickory, Tuscan Hills and Sterling Knight — four horses fighting for two or three spots two-to-three furlongs out is the single biggest source of traffic danger in this race and could compromise any or all of them.

Croupier — mapped to midfield due to redistribution but a genuine prominent racer; if he pushes forward and gets into a pace-burning battle for position, he risks flattering his early sectionals and fading when it matters.

Zarathos — has the form and going figures to be a serious factor but is entirely dependent on a clear run two out; the congested midfield increases the probability of him meeting trouble exactly when he needs to accelerate.

God Of War — 100-day absence for Tom Clover is worth monitoring in the paddock and early sections; if rusty, he may not produce his typical hold-up finish, but if he travels with intent, the race pace created by the prominent cluster sets up perfectly for him.

races.name: Racing Welfare Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Rogue Empire
runners_data.note: Two wins from two at 16f on good ground in recent starts are strong form credentials, but this horse is a natural hold-up type pushed to the lead by race circumstance — Roger Teal's yard is 0/10 in 14-day window and the style mismatch (STYLE_FIT=0.80) must temper confidence, even if the pace advantage is real.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in his last five starts, including back-to-back victories, mark Rogue Empire as a serious threat, and he returns fit on 21 days' rest with experience of today's trip and conditions; the risk is that ninth last time out leaves a question mark over his current form.

runners_data.name: Tarbat Ness
runners_data.note: The only runner not redistributed from its natural role in this race, settling comfortably in a tracking position; John Berry's 7-year-old has a strong course-distance profile (1W3P from 15 similar-going starts) and a 21-day break that mirrors a pattern before his best efforts, making him a natural danger if the leader weakens.
runners_data.comment: Tarbat Ness bounced back to winning form two starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, with 21 days since that unplaced run leaving him fresh enough to fire again; the concern is whether he can bounce back sharply enough from that latest blank.

runners_data.name: An Bradan Feasa
runners_data.note: Consistent placed performer at 16f on good ground (2-3-2-3-2 in last five), showing the stamina is genuine; Jack Jones has had one winner from 13 in the last 14 days, and although this horse's natural instinct is to come from further back, its STYLE_FIT of 0.93 means the midfield map position is only a slight compromise.
runners_data.comment: Consistent and clearly in fine nick after a run 13 days ago, An Bradan Feasa has placed in three consecutive outings and gets the better of his rivals on our rating; he has run over today's trip and going before, and the 138 lb burden is the sole reservation.

runners_data.name: Mio Amico
runners_data.note: Returning from 94 days off — the longest layoff of any runner in this field — which is the primary concern for the Michael Keady-trained 4-year-old; all five historical runs are on Flat/Soft surfaces at Southwell or Lingfield with no similar-going turf record, making the Good to Firm conditions at Newmarket a genuine unknown.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of seven on our figures and with a speed rating of 56 that does little to inspire, Mio Amico faces a stiff task after 94 days off, though he has run over today's distance and going before and does boast two wins in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Laravie
runners_data.note: James Owen's 7-year-old is in the form of his life (4 wins from 11 similar-going runs, 112243 recent form), handles visors, and has won and placed repeatedly at this trip on comparable going; naturally a hold-up type mapped into midfield, but his proximity to the front of that group and his course-fitness after a 13-day turnaround make him the strongest hold-up threat in the race.
runners_data.comment: Laravie arrives just 13 days fresh off a third, with two seconds and back-to-back wins deeper in her recent form, and experience over today's trip and going standing her in good stead; the risk is that she has not converted in her last two starts.

runners_data.name: Free World
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish, which is a significant concern over 2 miles on Good to Firm ground; won at 16f on good last time out but has a patchy record stepping back up in trip, and Ian Williams's 4/35 14-day strike rate offers little trainer backing — the fade warning and trip question make this a lower-confidence runner.
runners_data.comment: Free World won last time out and comes back on a quick ten-day turnaround, but ranked sixth of seven on our figures and officially rated just 60, he faces a stiff task against better-rated rivals; the experience over today's trip and going at least means conditions hold no surprises.

runners_data.name: The Craftymaster
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's 6-year-old carries headgear (t) and arrives with back-to-back wins at 16f (Goodwin and Southwell), giving genuine form at this distance; the 5/45 14-day trainer strike rate is modest but Myla Coppins on a 5lb claim adds value, and the lower OR of 57 means the weight advantage could matter if the race develops into a slog.
runners_data.comment: Twice a winner in his last six starts, including a victory last time out and a second two starts back, The Craftymaster arrives on a pleasing run of form; however, he carries 122 lb and our rating places him fifth of seven, suggesting he faces a stiff ask here.

races.paceDynamic: Rogue Empire is the sole confirmed front-runner here, redistributed to the lead as the most likely pace-setter despite being a natural hold-up horse, which means this 2m contest will be run at a genuinely sustainable, measured tempo rather than a pressured gallop. With no natural frontrunner to push the pace, Rogue Empire is likely to bowl along at a comfortable clip on Good to Firm ground, setting up a race that will be decided by stamina and finishing quality rather than a test of early speed. The bulk of the field — An Bradan Feasa, Mio Amico, Laravie, Free World, and The Craftymaster — are all true hold-up types redistributed into midfield positions because this field holds far more hold-up and prominent horses than the map can accommodate at the rear; of these, Laravie (4 wins from 11 similar-going runs, strong recent form) and An Bradan Feasa (consistent placed form at this trip and going) are best placed to secure a tracking position. A steady, uncontested pace on Good to Firm ground over 2m strongly favours horses with proven stamina at this trip and the ability to produce a sustained late run, making the hold-up-to-midfield closers with strong similar-going records the primary beneficiaries of this race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rogue Empire Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Rogue Empire is allowed to bowl along unchallenged at a comfortable gallop and the hold-up pack fails to organise a coherent challenge.
scenarios.body: Rogue Empire, racing out of its natural role but with two recent wins at 16f on good ground, could exploit a slow pace by controlling fractions and stealing enough of a lead that the hold-up pack runs out of track; this is the dominant shape because no genuine frontrunner exists to force a searching pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow enough that hold-up types tracking in midfield (An Bradan Feasa, Laravie) build momentum in the final quarter-mile and the leader flattens out.
scenarios.body: Laravie's consistent 2m form on good-to-firm ground and An Bradan Feasa's repeated placed efforts at this trip make them the most likely beneficiaries if the late rush materialises; the STYLE_FIT discount applies as these horses are racing closer than ideal, but their stamina profiles are genuine.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tarbat Ness Stalks and Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Tarbat Ness settles just off the pace in second or third and produces a sustained run from 3f out when Rogue Empire begins to tire.
scenarios.body: Tarbat Ness has a win and three places from 15 similar-going runs and is one of the few runners not redistributed from a different role, giving it a natural mid-prominent position to exploit; if Rogue Empire fades in the final furlong, Tarbat Ness has the positional advantage to pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Outsiders Land
scenarios.trigger: If the race unfolds in chaotic fashion — Rogue Empire stopping quickly and the hold-up pack suffering interference — and a lower-weighted runner at a big price catches the field napping.
scenarios.body: The Craftymaster (OR=57, two recent wins at 16f, headgear) or Free World (OR=60, won at 16f on good last time, handles the going) could sneak through if the race fractures and the market leaders fail to deliver; this scenario is unlikely given the clear pace picture but represents genuine tail-risk at big prices.

watchPoints.text: Rogue Empire — watch whether Owen Lewis (5lb claimer) elects to take the race by the scruff early or idles in front; if he is allowed to dictate a crawl, the hold-up pack will be crowding for position on the home turn.

Laravie's visor — headgear worn here and significant recent improvement in form; if Laravie tracks Rogue Empire closely rather than getting buried in the hold-up pack, it becomes a serious pace-shape beneficiary.

Mio Amico's 94-day absence on unfamiliar going — any sign of sluggishness or greenness in the first mile from this horse would effectively remove the second-biggest market threat from the race shape equation.

Free World's "fades in finish" tag over 2 miles on Good to Firm — watch the betting market; if punters support this horse despite the flag, it suggests insider confidence in fitness over the form read, which is worth noting.

The Craftymaster's weight advantage — at OR=57 with a 5lb claimer, this horse carries the lightest burden in the field; if the pace is truly slow and the race develops into a sprint finish, low weight could be decisive late on.
